title: Optimization Engineer, Grid Systems
description:
About Us
GridCARE is a leading venture-backed startup solving the most critical constraint in AI’s growth trajectory: immediate access to power. As demand for computing skyrockets, access to energy has become the defining bottleneck in the AI infrastructure race. While leading tech companies invest billions in speculative, long-term solutions that may take decades to arrive, GridCARE’s pioneering physics-based generative AI platform unlocks gigawatts of hidden capacity in today’s electric grid — enabling hyperscalers, data center developers, and utilities to power AI infrastructure years sooner than conventional approaches and without costly upgrades.
Founded at Stanford’s Doerr School of Sustainability and backed by leading investors, GridCARE has assembled a world-class team spanning power systems, AI, and infrastructure.
At GridCARE, you will:

- Work at the intersection of AI, energy, and infrastructure — the foundation of the next industrial revolution.

- Partner with hyperscalers, developers, and utilities on high-impact, real-world deployments.

- Help shape a more abundant, efficient, and resilient energy future for the digital era.

- Join a company defining a new category — capacity acceleration for AI.

- Receive competitive compensation, equity, and benefits in a fast-growth, mission-driven environment.

About the role
We're looking for an engineer in the early stages of their career who has demonstrated the ability to solve difficult technical problems in a professional or research setting to work on hard computational problems in the electric grid. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving difficult optimization problems and building software that has a direct impact on critical infrastructure. You’ll work closely with experienced engineers and researchers to build tools that help make the grid more flexible, efficient, and resilient as data centers, renewables, storage, and new regulations reshape how electricity systems operate.

What you’ll do

- Build optimization and simulation software for large-scale electric grid planning and operations problems.

- Develop models and algorithms for resource scheduling, network constraints, system reliability, and large-scale operational planning.

- Translate mathematical ideas into clear, tested, maintainable code.

- Analyze computational performance, identify bottlenecks, and improve reliability.

- Learn, customize, and fine-tune optimization algorithms.

- Work with real-world data and constraints from large physical systems.

- Collaborate across software engineering, applied AI, and power systems.

- Take ownership of important modeling and optimization challenges.

What we’re looking for

- A Master's degree or equivalent experience in a quantitative field such as engineering, computer science, applied math, physics, or operations research.

- Strong fundamentals in math, algorithms, and software engineering.

- Experience writing production-quality code in a language such as Python or Julia.

- Experience with optimization solvers, simulation tools, and large-scale numerical workflows.

- Ability to reason from first principles and learn unfamiliar technical areas quickly.

- Strong debugging, communication, and collaboration skills.

- Effectively leverage modern AI tools and workflows to accelerate model development, experimentation, and software engineering.

- 1–5 years of industry experience, or equivalent applied research experience, in optimization, modeling, simulation, or scientific software development.

Nice to have

- Exposure to power systems, energy markets, or the utility industry.

- Exposure to optimization, operations research, numerical methods, scientific computing, or large-scale infrastructure systems.

- Interest in electricity infrastructure, climate, energy, or industrial AI.

What We Offer

- Competitive salary, performance bonus, and equity.

- Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage.

- Lunch provided three days a week in office.

- Hybrid schedule: 3 days in office for collaboration, 2 days remote for focused work.

- Access to leading academic, industry, and government partners in the AI-energy ecosystem.

- A mission-driven team focused on shaping the future of the energy transition.

Salary Range
$140,000–$220,000
Join us in tackling one of the most important infrastructure challenges of our time - enabling the energy foundation for the age of AI.

title: Physical Systems Modeling Engineer
description:
Location: Redwood City, CA (Hybrid) or Remote – US
Team: Engineering
Type: Full-time
About GridCARE
GridCARE is a leading venture-backed startup solving the most critical constraint in AI’s growth trajectory: immediate access to power. At GridCARE, you will:

- Work at the intersection of AI, energy, and infrastructure — the foundation of the next industrial revolution.

- Partner with hyperscalers, developers, and utilities on high-impact, real-world deployments.

About the role
We are looking for a quantitative engineer to help build the models at the core of how GridCARE understands data center power: how facilities consume energy today, and how that consumption will evolve over time. In this role, you will develop simulation and forecasting models for existing and future data centers and the components inside data centers that will be used to support planning decisions across the full horizon, from intraday operations to multi-year infrastructure development. The goal is not simply to predict future demand, but to build models that can generate realistic future operating scenarios under a wide range of assumptions and conditions.
This role is well suited for someone who enjoys reasoning about complex systems, working with imperfect data, and translating real-world behavior into quantitative models. You should be excited to learn new domains and apply rigorous analytical thinking to difficult problems.
What you'll do

- Build models that accurately represent the physical systems inside of a data center

- Develop simulation frameworks that capture uncertainty, growth trajectories, and operational behavior across planning horizons.

- Explore how changes in technology, utilization, deployment strategies, and external factors influence future energy consumption.

- Analyze historical data to identify patterns, drivers, and sources of uncertainty.

- Evaluate model performance and continuously improve assumptions, methodologies, and predictive accuracy.

- Collaborate with engineers, researchers, and business stakeholders to translate practical questions into quantitative analyses.

- Communicate model assumptions, limitations, and findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Take ownership of key modeling components and drive them from concept through validation and deployment.

What we're looking for

- Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD in a quantitative field, with 1–5+ years of relevant industry or applied research experience.

- Experience working with data, mathematical models, simulations, forecasting problems, and time-series analysis.

- Experience with forecasting under uncertainty, probabilistic modeling, or scenario generation.

- A passion for understanding how data centers work and operate: their components, load behavior, operating constraints, and how that operation interacts with the electric grid.

- Proficiency in Python or a similar programming language.

- Ability to think from first principles and learn unfamiliar technical domains quickly.

- Comfort working with ambiguity and open-ended questions.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills.

- Demonstrated ability to effectively use AI tools in technical workflows.

Nice to have

- Exposure to infrastructure systems, energy systems, cloud computing, data centers, telecommunications networks, or other large-scale engineered systems.

- Exposure to data center, GPU, CPU power consumption modeling.

- Experience modeling data center to grid interaction, such as interconnection, load response, or capacity constraints.

- Experience developing models used to support real-world operational or planning decisions.

- Experience working with large datasets.

Why GridCARE

- Work on a problem that directly affects the speed of deploying AI and energy infrastructure

- Own technical direction on a product built from the ground up alongside domain experts

- Meaningful organizational influence in a small, high-trust team

- Competitive salary, equity, and benefits; hybrid in Redwood City with remote flexibility

Our Philosophy
We believe small teams of strong engineers can solve important, real-world infrastructure problems. We value clear thinking, strong ownership, pragmatic execution, and systems that hold up in production. If you're excited about technical leadership at the intersection of energy, infrastructure, and modern SaaS — we'd love to talk.
Salary Range
$140,000 – $250,000

title: Principal Power Systems Engineer
description:
Job Description
We are looking for a Principal Power Systems Engineer with hands-on interconnection study experience and a passion for improving the grid integration process through AI and automation . In this role, you will lead in-depth technical analyses, build out our dynamics and short-circuit duty study capability, analyze results, and present study findings directly to utilities and customers. You will serve as a technical subject-matter expert for the engineering team, and help lead the plan that connects planning-side capacity assessment to how utilities implement it in operations. You will work with utilities, developers, and regulators to accelerate interconnection timelines. This is a unique opportunity to combine deep power systems expertise and stakeholder engagement, with cutting-edge AI solutions to modernize how studies are performed.

Responsibilities

- Perform and lead load and generation interconnection studies, including steady-state, short-circuit, or dynamic analysis with widely accepted commercial tools.

- Build out GridCARE's approach to dynamics and short-circuit duty studies — defining the methodology and selecting cost-effective tooling so we can run these studies when they are required.

- Develop power flow and stability models to evaluate system impact for new interconnections, including data centers and renewable generation (inverter-based resources).

- Serve as a technical subject-matter expert for the engineering team, advising on study methodology and interconnection process questions.

- Help lead the plan that bridges planning and operations — translating capacity assessment and qualification into an approach utilities can actually implement in the operations plane.

- Collaborate directly with utilities, developers, and regulators to understand their needs and facilitate smooth interconnection processes and compliance with standards.

- Present study results, recommendations, and process findings directly to utility planners, project managers, and customer stakeholders.

- Evaluate interconnection options, system upgrades, and Grid-Enhancing Technologies (GETs), providing clear recommendations to stakeholders.

- Partner with AI and automation teams to streamline study processes and improve accuracy.

- Stay engaged with the latest interconnection news, standards, and emerging solutions in power systems, including the DOE i2X forum and ESIG modeling task force.

Qualifications
Required

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering (Power Systems focus) or a related field. Master's or PhD preferred.

- 10+ years of experience in power system studies, transmission planning, or interconnection, at a utility or a consulting firm.

- Demonstrated hands-on experience running interconnection studies specifically — a minimum of two years.

- Proficiency with commercial power system tools (e.g., PSSE, PSLF, PowerWorld, PSCAD, PowerGEM TARA, ASPEN).

- Strong coding skills in Python or equivalent, including use of power system tool APIs (psspy, simauto, pypowergem).

- Strong understanding of FERC, NERC, and ISO/RTO interconnection processes .

- Experience working with or for a utility transmission planning or interconnection team .

- Knowledge of steady-state and dynamic load modeling requirements.

- A creative, forward-looking approach to problem solving — someone who finds paths forward rather than stopping at the bottlenecks in current planning practice — with a bias toward action.

- Excellent problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills in a fast-paced startup environment, with a focus on client interaction.

Preferred

- Interconnection process experience across multiple regions, particularly ERCOT/Texas, the Midwest, or the Southeast.

- Working proficiency in Python or equivalent, including use of power system tool APIs (psspy, simauto, pypowergem).

- Experience in applying machine-learning and AI applications to power system studies.

- Able to leverage AI code development tools such as Cursor, Copilot and Claude Code to accelerate development.

- Experience deploying power system applications in the cloud.

- Familiarity with version control (git) and basic software engineering practices.

- Ability to write well-documented, tested, and maintainable code.

What We Offer

- Competitive salary and equity.

- Comprehensive benefits package.

- Hybrid work environment with catered lunches and snacks.

- The chance to work at the intersection of AI, automation, and power systems alongside experienced engineers and leading researchers.

title: Power Operations Desk Operator
description:
GridCARE accelerates power for AI. We help data centers connect to the grid years faster by identifying available capacity and operationalizing flexible interconnections, and we help utilities serve large loads without compromising reliability. Our Power Operations platform provides real-time monitoring and dispatch, drives long-term energy management and system optimization, and seamlessly connects utility planning, utility operations, and data center operations. It builds on decades of experience deploying best-in-class DERMS and virtual power plants at AutoGrid.
Learn more about GridCARE:

- TechCrunch: GridCARE thinks more than 100 GW of data-center capacity is hiding in the grid

- Utility Dive: Portland General Electric invests in AI-powered flexibility to speed data-center connection

- Data Center Dynamics: From Years to Months — Creating an AI Fast Lane for Data Centers

- GridCARE Raises $64 Million Series A to Create a New Category: Power Acceleration

THE ROLE
Where flexible interconnections become real
Our Johnson City Operations Center is where flexible interconnections become real. As a Power Operations Desk Operator, you will staff a 24/7 desk that monitors data center loads, on-site generation, and grid conditions in real time, and you will execute the curtailment and dispatch actions that keep those sites within their interconnection agreements. You are the person utilities and site teams call when conditions change, and the person who makes sure nothing gets missed at 3 a.m. This role reports to the Director of 24/7 & Customer Support Operations.
We are hiring at multiple levels, from trainable early-career operators to seasoned control room professionals. Your title, responsibilities, and pay will match your experience.

RESPONSIBILITIES
What you'll do

- Monitor real-time telemetry (load, generation, frequency, voltage, and grid signals) across a fleet of data center sites and flexible interconnection assets.

- Execute dispatch and curtailment instructions from utilities and ISOs/RTOs within contractual response windows, and verify that sites respond as expected.

- Follow, and help improve, operating procedures, checklists, and escalation paths; document every action in the shift log.

- Coordinate over phone, radio, and chat with utility control centers, data center facility teams, and GridCARE engineering during normal and abnormal conditions.

- Identify alarms, anomalies, and data quality issues early; troubleshoot with the field and software teams and escalate when needed.

- Conduct thorough shift turnovers so the incoming operator has full situational awareness.

- Participate in drills, post-event reviews, and continuous improvement of the operations desk.

- Senior operators: mentor junior staff, lead complex events, and serve as a subject matter expert on utility interconnection and market operations.

QUALIFICATIONS
Required at all levels

- Ability to work a fixed 12-hour day or fixed 12-hour night schedule, including weekends and holidays, on-site in Johnson City, TN.

- Strong situational awareness, attention to detail, and the discipline to follow procedures exactly, especially under pressure.

- Clear, professional communication over the phone and in writing.

- Comfort working with software dashboards, alarm systems, and spreadsheets; ability to learn new tools quickly.

- High school diploma or equivalent. Offers for this position are contingent on a background check and a pre-employment drug screen.

Operator I / II (0–5 years)

- Candidates with a technical or military background, or an associate's degree in electrical, energy, or a related field, will stand out.

- Interest in the power grid and a desire to earn industry certifications on the job.

Senior Operator (5+ years)

- Experience in a utility control room, generation dispatch, NOC, or a similar 24/7 operations environment.

- Working knowledge of SCADA/EMS systems, demand response, or DER/DERMS operations.

- Familiarity with ISO/RTO market and reliability operations (PJM, MISO, TVA, ERCOT, or similar).

- NERC System Operator certification is valued but not required.

SCHEDULE
Twelve-hour shifts on a 2-2-3 rotation

- Rotation. Two on, two off, three on, then the reverse. Seven 12-hour shifts every two weeks, never more than three in a row, and every other weekend off as a three-day weekend.

- Fixed assignment. You are hired into a fixed day shift (6:00 AM – 6:00 PM) or a fixed night shift (6:00 PM – 6:00 AM); days and nights do not rotate. Tell us your preference when you apply.

- Hours. The desk is staffed 24/7/365, including weekends and holidays. Overtime is built into the schedule and paid at 1.5x, and night-shift operators receive a $3.00/hr differential.

COMPENSATION
Placement within a range depends on directly relevant experience and certifications. Overtime and night differential are paid on top.
Pay by level
OPERATOR I: 0–2 yrs · trainable, strong aptitude

- $24 – $29 /hr

OPERATOR II: 2–5 yrs · dispatch, NOC, or SCADA

- $29 – $36 /hr

SENIOR OPERATOR: 5+ yrs · NERC cert or utility control room

- $38 – $48 /hr

BENEFITS
What else you get

- Medical, dental, and vision coverage, and a 401(k) retirement plan.

- Flexible paid time off, scheduled with your manager so the desk stays covered.

- Twelve observed holidays plus two floating holidays. Because the desk never closes, operators receive holiday pay whether the holiday falls on a shift or a day off, with additional pay for holidays worked.

- Equity in a fast-growing company at the center of the AI power buildout.

- Paid training, with support for NERC certification and continuing education.

Join us in tackling one of the most important infrastructure challenges of our time — enabling the energy foundation for the age of AI.
